dayShape: lab day (virtual, replaces the real second-law lab)
floor: Every student completes the regular-level standard (T5): state in words, with numbers from their own tables, how acceleration changes when the fan force doubles and when the mass doubles. Bands are hidden. The top band is this standard.

clock.afterHuddle2: 1/m graph, then predict and run 3 bars (about 5 min)
clock.note: Lab day: huddle 2 comes after the data at minute 28, not 25. Code 2 is never blocked by record state: a student who is behind still gets the huddle.

gates.huddle1Code: the door stays shut until the pre-lab is done (existing mechanic); code 1 is given by Mr. D at the end of huddle 1 and ends the hold screen
gates.huddle2Code: entered at the end of huddle 2. It unlocks the 1/m axis, the test run and the exit ticket. It is not blocked by an unfinished table. Mr. D decides who is ready by reading the room.
gates.holdScreen: Huddle 1 shows a hold screen with the step card. Huddle 2 shows the formalizing tab (huddle2Tab below) with the write-on blanks.

prelab.note: This is the 3-minute warm-up: three easy picture items, review only, then one prediction.

questions.picture: a cart with a long arrow pointing right and a short arrow pointing left
questions.q: Which way does the net force point?
questions.explain: The longer arrow wins, so the net force points right.

questions.picture: two straight speed graphs from 0: line A climbs steeply, line B climbs gently
questions.explain: A steeper line means the speed grows faster.

questions.picture: a cart with two equal arrows pointing opposite ways
options: keeps its speed, or stays at rest
questions.explain: Equal arrows cancel, so the net force is zero.

prediction.q: A cart is pushed with a steady push. You make the push twice as strong. The acceleration will be:
prediction.afterTry: Good. You will test this in the lab.
prediction.note: Do not reveal the answer here. The lab shows it. Log the choice.

stepCard.title: Step card
steps: Go to the shelf and take four mass bars.
At the balance, read the mass of the cart and of one bar.
At the track, load 2 bars on the cart. The mass is the cart plus the bars.
Set a fan setting and press Run.
Place the two markers far apart on the straight part of the speed graph. Read the acceleration.
Part 1: keep 2 bars. Run fan settings 1, 2, 3 and 4. Record each.
Predict, then Part 2: set the fan to 3 and run 0, 1, 2 and 4 bars. Record each.
Graph acceleration against fan force, then against mass.
Write your claim, evidence and reasoning. Use numbers from your tables.
afterCode2: Use your line to predict the acceleration with 3 bars. Then run it.

quests.text: Go through the door into the lab
quests.hint: The light on the DOOR turns green when the pre-lab is done.

quests.text: Take four mass bars from the BAR SHELF
quests.hint: Walk to the BAR SHELF, face it and press E. Take four bars.

quests.text: Read the mass of the cart and of one bar on the BALANCE
quests.hint: The BALANCE is the small scale on the bench. Press E and read both masses.
It is the long rail with the cart on it. Face it and press E.

quests.text: Load 2 bars, pick fan setting 2 and press Run
quests.hint: Use the bar buttons to load 2 bars. Pick setting 2. Press Run and watch the speed graph.

quests.text: Place both markers on the straight part of the speed graph and read the acceleration
quests.hint: Drag the two markers far apart on the dots. The box shows the acceleration in m/s².

quests.text: Record the run: type the mass, then press Record
quests.hint: The mass is 0.50 kg for the cart plus 0.25 kg for each bar. The fan force and the acceleration fill in for you.

quests.text: Part 1: keep 2 bars and record fan settings 1, 2, 3 and 4
quests.hint: Change only the fan setting. Run, read, record. Four rows.

quests.text: Predict what a bigger mass does to the acceleration (one try)
quests.hint: Part 2 stays locked until you answer. There is no wrong answer to log.

quests.text: Part 2: set the fan to 3 and record 0, 1, 2 and 4 bars
quests.hint: Change only the number of bars. The mass is 0.50 kg plus 0.25 kg for each bar.
In the graph builder pick fan force across and acceleration up. Press Guide line.
Pick mass across and acceleration up. If the dots bend, press Connect the dots.

quests.text: Write your claim, evidence and reasoning
quests.hint: Use two numbers from each table. Open the checklist.
Mr. D gives code 2 at the end of huddle 2.
Pick 1/m across and acceleration up. Press Guide line. The line passes through the corner.

quests.text: Predict the acceleration with 3 bars from your line (one try), then run it
quests.hint: 3 bars is 1.25 kg. Find 1/m for 1.25 kg, then read up to the line.
Press Hand in on the notebook.

record.studentTypes: mass (kg). Accepted within 0.01 of 0.50 + 0.25 × bars. A wrong mass shows: The cart is 0.50 kg and each bar adds 0.25 kg.
record.readingRule: Markers closer than 0.5 s apart show: Spread the markers apart. A short stretch is shaky. No reading is given.

messages.predictLock: Predict first. The Run button opens when you answer.
messages.markersClose: Spread the markers apart. A short stretch is shaky.
messages.massWrong: The cart is 0.50 kg and each bar adds 0.25 kg.
messages.needBars: Take the mass bars from the shelf first.
messages.guideLineNeedsDots: Record at least three runs for this graph first.
messages.codeAsk: Mr. D gives you the code.
messages.tableGood: Your table has all four rows.

predictions.q: A cart is pushed with a steady push. You make the push twice as strong. The acceleration will be:
You double the mass and keep the fan force. The acceleration will be:
predictions.log: choice only; one try; no hint on a wrong choice

predictions.q: Use your line. What acceleration will 3 bars give?
predictions.log: typed value and the run result

figures.title: The fan cart on the track
figures.oneMark: each part is labeled: fan, cart, bars on top, track, motion sensor at the far end, force sensor on the fan
figures.lookFirst: the fan on top of the cart and the bars sitting on the cart
figures.wrongReading: thinking something pulls the cart: nothing pulls it, the fan pushes it

figures.title: The speed graph from one run
figures.axes: across: time in seconds, 0 to 2.0. Up: speed in m/s.
figures.oneMark: one dot is one reading of the cart's speed at one moment
figures.lookFirst: whether the dots climb in a straight line, and how steep it is
figures.wrongReading: reading the height of the last dot as the acceleration: that is the final speed. Acceleration is how much the speed grows each second.

figures.title: Acceleration against fan force (Part 1)
figures.axes: across: fan force in N. Up: acceleration in m/s².
figures.oneMark: one dot is one run: the fan force and the acceleration it gave
figures.lookFirst: do the dots climb, and do they sit near a straight line?
figures.wrongReading: reading a dot's height as a fan force: height is acceleration

figures.title: Acceleration against mass (Part 2)
figures.axes: across: mass in kg. Up: acceleration in m/s².
figures.oneMark: one dot is one run at one mass, with the fan force fixed
figures.lookFirst: do the dots fall, and do they fall straight or bend?
figures.wrongReading: calling it a straight line because the first two dots look straight: look at all four

figures.title: Acceleration against 1/m
figures.axes: across: 1/m, which is one divided by the mass, in per kg. Up: acceleration in m/s².
figures.oneMark: one dot is one run: its 1/m and its acceleration
figures.lookFirst: do the dots sit on a straight line that passes through the corner?
figures.wrongReading: reading 1/m as the mass: a heavy cart has a small 1/m

tutorial1.name: Read the speed graph
captions: The motion sensor draws the cart's speed as it rolls.
Each dot is one reading of the speed.
A steeper line means the speed grows faster.
Drag the two markers far apart on the dots. The box shows the acceleration.
Markers close together give a shaky reading, so spread them out.

tutorial2.name: Build a graph
captions: Pick what goes across and what goes up.
Every row in your table adds one dot.
Press Guide line to draw the straight line through the dots.
If the dots bend, press Connect the dots instead.

postlab.prompt: How does the cart's acceleration change when the fan force doubles? When the mass doubles? Use numbers from your tables.

claim: When the fan force doubles, the acceleration
When the mass doubles, the acceleration
reasoning: This evidence supports my claim because
The numbers are not exact because

checklist: My claim answers both parts: the fan force and the mass.
My evidence has two numbers from Part 1 and two from Part 2.
I say about double and about half, not exactly.
My reasoning says why the numbers point to my claim.

huddle2Tab.tested: What will be tested: say how acceleration changes when the fan force doubles and when the mass doubles, using numbers from a table. Read a straight line to predict a new acceleration.

blanks.text: Double the fan force, same cart: the acceleration is about ______.
Double the mass, same fan force: the acceleration is about ______.
Acceleration against 1/m is a ______ line through the corner.

worked.problem: A 1.00 kg cart at fan force 0.15 N has acceleration 0.14 m/s². Predict the acceleration at 0.45 N.
steps: Check: your table says about 0.44. Close.

worked.problem: A 0.50 kg cart at 0.45 N has acceleration 0.88 m/s². Predict the acceleration of a 1.50 kg cart at 0.45 N.
steps: Three times the mass gives one third the acceleration.

worked.problem: On your acceleration-against-1/m line, 1/m = 1.00 per kg gives 0.44 m/s². Predict the acceleration of a 1.25 kg cart.
steps: The line passes through the corner, so 0.80 gives 0.80 × 0.44 m/s².

crux.q: Same cart, the fan force triples. About how many times bigger is the acceleration?
Same fan force, the mass triples. What happens to the acceleration?
Which of your graphs are straight lines?
crux.answer: acceleration against fan force, and acceleration against 1/m. Not acceleration against mass.

mrDSays: friction: the track has a tiny drag. That is why the force line misses the corner by a hair.
1/m: one divided by the mass. Per kg.
huddle2Tab.note: Mr. D does these on the pen display. The site shows the blanks and the answers after he finishes. ΣF = ma and the newton are slot 8.

exit.prompt: Draw two small graphs, both with acceleration going up. On the first put fan force across. On the second put mass across, with the fan force fixed. Sketch the dots and label the axes.
look: first graph: dots climb in a straight line from near the corner
second graph: dots fall, steep at first and then flatter
axes labeled with the quantity on each
